newsitem.title: USA: "Suspicious packages" found at U.S. Press Club.
newsitem.headline: "Suspicious packages" found at U.S. Press Club.

text.p: Police removed two "suspicious packages" from the U.S. National Press Club building on Thursday, hours after detonating two letter bombs sent to the Washington offices of a Saudi-owned newspaper.

Police said the press club building, which houses the Washington offices of many U.S. and foreign news organisations and is two blocks from the White House, was partially evacuated after discovery of the second pair of "packages."
The first two bombs were discovered by an employee of the newspaper Al-Hayat as he was opening the morning mail, Washington police said in a statement, adding that they were harmlessly destroyed.
The third and fourth devices, described as "suspicious packages" by Washington police spokesman Officer Anthony O'Leary, were removed from the site around 4 p.m. EST (2100 GMT).
Washington police and the FBI's Terrorist Task Force were investigating the case.
Al-Hayat, a Saudi newspaper based in London, had published the manifesto of a radical Islamic group after the fatal June 25 bombing of U.S. military personnel in the Saudi city of Khobar.
